Definition: of foreign origin; Candacè, an Egyptian queen:--Candace.
BiblicalUsage: Candace is the title of the queen of Ethiopia, and the name by which Luke calls her — the queen under whom the Ethiopian eunuch served as treasurer. He had come to Jerusalem to worship and was reading Isaiah on the road home when Philip met him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Candace matters because her servant's conversion opened the gospel to a new continent. The queen never met Philip, but her treasurer carried the gospel home to Ethiopia, and the church there traces its faith to that chariot.
